verses.text: "How terrible for the rebellious children," says the LORD, "who carry out plans that are not mine, who make agreements without my Spirit, adding sin to sin.
They go down to Egypt without asking me. They look for help from Pharaoh's strength and hide in Egypt's shadow.
But Pharaoh's strength will bring you shame, and hiding in Egypt's shadow will bring you disgrace.
Though Judah's officials are in Zoan and their messengers have arrived in Hanes,
everyone will be put to shame because of a people who cannot help them. Egypt brings no help and no benefit, only shame and disgrace."

This is the message of judgment about the animals of the Negev. Through a land of trouble and danger, of lionesses and lions, of poisonous snakes and fiery flying serpents, the messengers carry their riches on the backs of donkeys and their treasures on the humps of camels, to a people who cannot help them.
Egypt's help is useless and empty. So I call her Rahab the Do Nothing.
Now go, write this on a tablet in front of them, and write it in a book, so that it will be a witness for the days to come, forever and ever.
For these are rebellious people, lying children, children who refuse to listen to the LORD's teaching.
They say to the seers, "Stop seeing visions!" and to the prophets, "Do not tell us what is right. Tell us nice things. Prophesy lies.
Get out of our way. Leave the path. Stop telling us about the Holy One of Israel!"
So this is what the Holy One of Israel says: "You have rejected this message. You trust in cruelty and lies, and you depend on them.
So this sin will be like a crack in a high wall, bulging out and about to fall. It will crash down suddenly, in an instant.
It will be smashed like a clay pot, broken so completely that not one piece is left big enough to carry coals from a fire or to scoop water from a well."
This is what the Lord GOD, the Holy One of Israel, says: "You will be saved by turning back to me and resting in me. Your strength will come from being calm and trusting me." But you would not do it.
You said, "No, we will run away on horses." So you will run away! You said, "We will ride on fast horses." So those who chase you will be fast!
A thousand of you will run away from the threat of one enemy. At the threat of five, you will all run away, until you are left like a flagpole on a mountaintop, like a flag on a hill.
Yet the LORD is waiting to be kind to you. He rises up to show you mercy. For the LORD is a God of justice. Blessed are all who wait for him.
You people of Zion who live in Jerusalem, you will weep no more. He will surely be kind to you when you cry for help. As soon as he hears you, he will answer you.
Though the Lord gives you the bread of trouble and the water of suffering, your teacher will not hide anymore. You will see your teacher with your own eyes.
Whether you turn to the right or to the left, your ears will hear a voice behind you saying, "This is the way. Walk in it."
Then you will treat your silver covered idols and your gold covered images as unclean. You will throw them away like dirty rags and say to them, "Go away!"
He will send rain for the seed you plant in the ground, and the food that comes from the land will be rich and plenty. On that day your cattle will graze in wide pastures.
The oxen and donkeys that work the soil will eat good feed, spread out with fork and shovel.
On the day of great slaughter, when the towers fall, streams of water will flow on every high mountain and every tall hill.

The moon will shine as brightly as the sun, and the sun will shine seven times brighter, like the light of seven full days, on the day the LORD bandages his people's injuries and heals the wounds he gave them.
Look, the name of the LORD is coming from far away, burning with anger, in thick rising smoke. His lips are full of fury, and his tongue is like a fire that burns everything.
His breath is like a rushing flood that rises up to the neck. He will shake the nations in the sieve of destruction. He will put a bit in the mouths of the peoples that leads them to ruin.
But you will sing as on the night of a holy festival. Your hearts will be glad, like people walking to the music of flutes on their way to the mountain of the LORD, to the Rock of Israel.
The LORD will make people hear his majestic voice. He will show his arm coming down in raging anger, with flames of fire that burn everything, with cloudburst, storm, and hailstones.
The voice of the LORD will shatter Assyria. He will strike them with his rod.
Every blow the LORD strikes on them with his punishing rod will be to the music of tambourines and harps, as he fights them in battle with his raised arm.

For a burning place has long been ready. Yes, it has been prepared for the king. Its fire pit has been made deep and wide, with plenty of fire and wood. The breath of the LORD, like a stream of burning sulfur, sets it on fire.
